title: GeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a convex real-valued function on a complete real inner-product space E. A global minimizer xstar exists with ‖x0 − xstar‖ ≤ R and f(x0) − f(xstar) ≤ Δ. Strong convexity is not required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: Public; spec.admissible, ConvexOn and minimizer clauses.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: A query x ∈ E returns exactly ∇f(x) for every call index and oracle seed. No function values or Hessians are returned. Gradient uniqueness eliminates any seed-dependent gradient error; no sampling or independence assumption is needed.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply and spec.admissible, HasGradientAt clause; LongTails/Template.lean: Oracle.answer and execute.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient map is Fréchet differentiable everywhere and satisfies ‖D(∇f)(x)‖ ≤ L0 + L1‖∇f(x)‖ for every x ∈ E, with L0 > 0 and L1 ≥ 0. Continuity of its derivative is not explicitly required.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.valid and spec.admissible, Differentiable and fderiv clauses.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E may be an infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space. E, L0, L1, R, Δ and x0 are public, with R > 0 and Δ > 0. The objective and minimizer are hidden. ε > 0 is excluded from publicInput, so the algorithm is independent of ε, while its prescribed execution budget depends on ε.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput and spec.valid; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm and budget.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a point in E satisfying f(output) − f(xstar) ≤ ε for a global minimizer xstar. No gradient-norm or distance accuracy is required.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: One global minimizer xstar witnesses the objective-gap guarantee almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law. Oracle cost is bounded by the prescribed budget for every seed.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.successful, ∃ xstar and ∀ᵐ clauses; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence, seedwise cost bound and product probability law.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup uses gradient-dependent curvature rather than a uniform Lipschitz-gradient bound, permits arbitrary real Hilbert spaces, and requires an accuracy-independent algorithm with a fixed seedwise oracle budget and almost-sure objective-gap accuracy.

descriptionHtml:
Generalized Smooth Convex Minimization

We consider minimizing a convex function f:E→R on a real Hilbert space E. The function f is (L0,L1)-smooth, with L0>0 and L1≥0, and has an everywhere differentiable gradient. A given point x0∈E satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R and f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ for a global minimizer x⋆, where R,Δ>0. The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm. The algorithm receives E, L0, L1, R, Δ, and x0; the tolerance ε may enter the oracle-call budget but is not an algorithm input.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity). For every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y).

Assumption 2 (Generalized smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, and its gradient ∇f:E→E is Fréchet differentiable everywhere. Its Hessian ∇2f(x):E→E satisfies ∥∇2f(x)∥op≤L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥,x∈E.

Assumption 3 (Minimizer and initialization). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ.

Queries may be made at any point of E. After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
Convex f:E→R on a real Hilbert space has a differentiable gradient satisfying ∥∇2f(x)∥≤L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥ everywhere. A minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R and f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ, with L0,R,Δ,ε>0 and L1≥0. Exact gradients are available; L0,L1,R,Δ are public inputs. The target is f(xout)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely; our constructions guarantee it for every seed. The setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import LongTails.Template

namespace LongTails.Setups.GeneralizedSmoothAndConvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE

structure Params extends Public where
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ q.L1 ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 < q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f oracle :=
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
    (∀ k seed x, HasGradientAt f (oracle.answer k (0, x) seed) x) ∧
    (∀ k seed, Differentiable ℝ (fun x => oracle.answer k (0, x) seed)) ∧
    (∀ k seed x, ‖fderiv ℝ (fun y => oracle.answer k (0, y) seed) x‖ ≤
      q.L0 + q.L1 * ‖oracle.answer k (0, x) seed‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R ∧
      f q.x0 - f xstar ≤ q.Δ)
  successful q f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.GeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
